execution_context.file_location: malicious macro in Word document attached to phishing email

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
AutoOpen()
  ' Malicious macro code here
  ' Downloads and executes Zeus Sphinx payload
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the Word document and enables macros, the macro executes, downloads the Zeus Sphinx banking trojan from a remote server, and runs it on the victim's machine, leading to credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros in unsolicited documents that download and execute binaries are a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents should not contain macros that download and execute external code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise automation uses macros to fetch data, but never to download and execute untrusted binaries.

execution_context.file_location: PowerShell command executed via HID emulation from USB device

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon USB insertion, the device emulates keyboard input to launch PowerShell, which downloads and executes a remote script, initiating the FIN7 infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: USB devices that emulate keyboard input to run PowerShell are a known malware delivery vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal USB devices should not inject keystrokes to execute code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, legitimate USB devices may automate setup, but not to download and run remote scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user submits a payment form, the code intercepts credit card data and exfiltrates it to a remote server controlled by attackers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating payment data is a hallmark of Magecart skimmers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not send sensitive payment data to third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Payment processors may send data to their own servers, but not to unknown domains.
key_indicators: Form data exfiltration to external domain

attack_chain.action: Victim receives phishing email with password-protected Word document containing malicious macro.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of macro and download of Zeus Sphinx trojan

attack_chain.action: User opens document and enables macros, triggering download and execution of banking trojan.
Victim receives USB device in the mail, which emulates keyboard input to launch PowerShell and download malware.
Malicious JavaScript is injected into e-commerce checkout pages, skimming credit card data at runtime.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of payment data to attacker

behavioral_signatures: Macros in Office documents that download and execute binaries
PowerShell launched via HID/keyboard emulation from USB devices
JavaScript on payment pages exfiltrating form data to unknown domains
file_indicators: Unexpected PowerShell execution from USB insertion
Injected JavaScript on e-commerce checkout pages
network_indicators: Connections to known malware C2 domains (e.g., Zeus Sphinx, FIN7, Magecart infrastructure)
POST requests from browser to non-payment domains during checkout
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that initiate network connections or drop executables. Detect PowerShell processes launched shortly after USB device insertion, especially those that download remote scripts. Inspect e-commerce sites for unauthorized JavaScript that sends payment data to external domains. Use network monitoring to flag suspicious outbound connections to known malicious infrastructure.
